subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron runs get an explicit `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or keep the current per-job `toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards model?
rationale: The next step defines a scheduled-run tool-access boundary and a new config/default precedence contract, which automation cannot choose safely without maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Add explicit cron policy
options.body: Add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, plus focused cron delivery regression tests.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Make cron sessions reuse `tools.subagents.tools` semantics, accepting a simpler config surface but documenting compatibility impact on existing jobs.

options.title: Keep current model
options.body: Decline the new config surface and document per-job `--tools`, creator-surface capture, and delivery safeguards as the supported mitigation.

recommendation.title: Add explicit cron policy
recommendation.body: Add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, plus focused cron delivery regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete wrote the prior detailed issue review and has the strongest recent history around cron runtime and tool-policy test seams.
